business_rules.statement: The Command Center board refresh defaults to 60 seconds, may be set to a 30-second per-tenant floor, and permits a faster interval only after validation against the deployment's scale.
No Frontline interaction on the worker's critical path blocks on a network operation, except the forced sync before designated high-risk actions.
Every reading surface that can be stale carries an explicit data-as-of or last-synced marker.

First fallback under overload: shed load in reverse order of safety importance — report generation and analytics first, agent operations second, oversight refresh third; capture ingestion and command delivery are shed last, and only into a durable queue.
A refused sync attempt never loses a capture; the device retains it in its durable queue and retries with backoff and jitter.
The sync-conflict panel caps its visible list at scale, most recent first, with a count.
A total platform outage does not stop on-device execution, deterministic detection, severity classification, Severity 1 lot freezing, or local containment.
No document, interface or client-facing material states an availability, Recovery Time Objective or Recovery Point Objective figure before DEC-NFR-002 is decided.

Four things stop during an outage and cannot be worked around locally: a Severity 1 hold cannot be released; a qualification clearance cannot be granted; a sign-off cannot be performed; and no new work can be published or assigned.
The trust window is tenant-settable below the 72-hour ceiling and an out-of-bound value is rejected at entry with the bound stated.
A device timestamp outside the clock-skew threshold never orders a write; the event routes to human resolution and is audited.
Media is evicted only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on an attempted upload.
No capture state is ever displayed as a single "synced" label; the distinct capture states are shown.
Evidence is immutable at creation; every correction is an append-only annotation carrying who, when and what changed; the original is unaltered.
No path deletes operational data outside the compliance-erasure workflow; shortening a retention horizon changes tier only.
A run finishes on the workflow version it started on, and that version is resolvable from the record for its full retention term.
The audit log is never shorter-lived than the tenant data it evidences.
An unretrievable or inconsistent record is reported as an integrity exception and never silently repaired or omitted.
A derived decision record persists with the operational record for its full term, beyond the 24-month trace horizon.
Zero-tolerance security rows are verified as zero, not as "within tolerance". A single cross-tenant row is a release blocker.
No state anywhere in the Frontline Worker Application is communicated by audio alone, and no audio cue is required for any safety-relevant state.
Every safety-relevant state — deviation, severity, hold, gate block, parked run, sync state — is represented persistently and visually until acknowledged or superseded.
No worker task requires navigating a menu tree; the application presents six destinations with one dominant.
A locale pack or content version with untranslated keys fails publication.
No string anywhere on any surface is machine-translated at runtime.
Engineering units in specification limits are never converted for display in any locale.

Fallback of fallback for a missing key detected at runtime: the device shows the key's identifier rather than a wrong-language string. Showing an identifier is ugly and honest; showing the other language is dangerous.
The deterministic safety layer executes correctly on every conformant device, on both operating systems, including the rugged Android class.
No telemetry, log or metric contains tenant operational content.
A telemetry gap is displayed as unknown, never as zero.
Qualification-expiry warnings may be configured earlier than 14 / 7 / 1 / 0 days and never later.
The run auto-close transition is the only automatic state transition on the platform.
No published version is ever edited in place; correction is by superseding version.
An in-flight run is never re-based; it finishes on the version it started on.
The tenant-configuration registry rejects an out-of-bound value at entry with the bound stated, and never accepts and logs it.
Every setting category is an approvable object and nothing applies silently.

Non-functional trade-off ordering, highest priority first: 1 Worker safety and the deterministic layer; 2 Tenant isolation; 3 Auditability; 4 Data integrity and durability; 5 Authorization and approval controls; 6 Honest communication; 7 Offline endurance; 8 Usability under floor conditions; 9 Availability of the web surfaces; 10 Performance and freshness; 11 Cost efficiency.
No design decision trades against the deterministic safety layer, tenant isolation, or auditability on performance or cost grounds.
No service-level, Recovery Time Objective, Recovery Point Objective, concurrency, throughput, device-count, tenant-count or latency figure appears anywhere in this blueprint as a commitment.
Every critical fallback must be observable, and no degraded state may remain silent.
No observability view, alert, dashboard, or export in the platform console exposes record-level operational content outside a support session, the compliance-emergency path, or a JBS access grant.
No metric, alert, or dashboard is accepted as audit evidence anywhere in the platform; every audit query resolves against the append-only tenant audit log.
business_rules.applies_to: investigations, disputes, regulatory response, tenant communication

business_rules.statement: Observability cardinality rule: permitted dimensions are tenant identifier, Site, Area, surface, module, device identifier, agent identifier, atom identifier, router role, Schedule Definition identifier, workflow identifier with version, package version, application version, server version, severity level, channel, access class, outcome status. Prohibited: Unit or serial identifier, Lot identifier, Run identifier, Step Execution identifier, Data Capture identifier, worker identity, free-text reason strings, any authored content value.
business_rules.enforcement_point: cardinality allow-list validated at emission; failure at build time

business_rules.statement: Every telemetry emission is validated against the cardinality allow-list, and an emission carrying a prohibited dimension fails the build rather than being dropped at runtime.
An audit-write failure causes the originating action to be refused with a stated reason and never causes the audit record to be queued or dropped.
Device state is computed on the four-state ladder, and a device with staged work and no heartbeat inside the trust window is reported as offline-expected rather than as a fault.
No fleet-wide destructive action can be initiated while the signal layer it depends on is marked missing or derived.
Every surface that displays sync state uses the distinct capture and command state names; the word "synced" appears as a state name nowhere in the product.
A capture from a skew-flagged device never resolves a conflict by device timestamp; it routes to the Command Center conflict-and-skew review.

No scheduled occurrence may produce an official effect twice. Official effects include finishing a run record, tiering data, anonymising worker identity, publishing a Lane B patch version, and sending a notification. Duplicate suppression is enforced by an idempotency key derived from the Schedule Definition identifier and the occurrence's due moment.
A Worker holding an expired lease cannot write; the storage layer rejects the write on the fencing token, and the rejection is recorded.
Anonymisation and tiering occurrences are never resumed after a failure without a completed reconciliation report attached to the resume approval.
Propagation delay is reported per surface, and the Frontline figure derives solely from device acknowledgement, never from an estimate or a server-side proxy.
No artificial-intelligence health view exposes a confidence value used as a gate, and the drift canary's last result and named owner are always displayed.
No alert on the platform is the sole mechanism enforcing safety, a hold, qualification, authorization, approval, suspension, or a device command.
Invariant alerts cannot be suppressed, rate-limited, or disabled by any account including the root, and an attempt to do so is refused and audited.
Controls whose values have no source in the Statement of Work display an awaiting-decision state and cannot be saved with a fabricated value in a production environment.
No read of tenant operational content occurs before the tenant banner is confirmed displayed and the session-open event is committed to the tenant's audit stream.
A normal support session offers no write capability of any kind; every mutating control is absent rather than disabled-with-a-tooltip.
All three access classes appear identically in the tenant's Platform Access History, and no filter or export can omit a class.
No platform role can perform any of the ten Command Center operational actions in any tenant, in any access class, including the compliance-emergency path.
Every incident record carries a classification, a named role owner, a detection source, a communication decision, and a verification checklist, and cannot be closed with any of them absent.
Recovery verification requires positive evidence for each item, and an incident cannot be closed on the absence of alerts alone.
An emergency pause never alters on-device specification gates, severity classification, the Severity 1 hold, or containment checklist launch.
No capability becomes live by being deployed; enablement requires passing evaluation scenarios plus an audited submission and approval.
No rollout and no rollback may produce a duplicate official effect, and no version change may reach a worker inside a run.
No deployment path can enable a capability whose evaluation scenarios have not passed, and no account including the root can bypass the gate.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with the floor named, and is never stored or logged as accepted.
business_rules.applies_to: Schedule Definitions and all configurable values

business_rules.statement: Activating a new definition version never rewrites, re-runs, or reclassifies any past occurrence.
Fencing is enforced by the storage layer, not by the worker. Any design in which the worker checks its own lease before writing is unsafe, because the check and the write are not atomic.
Exactly one Scheduler Controller instance holds the leader lease at any moment, and a passive instance creates no occurrences under any condition.
A capture is always validated against the workflow definition version it references, never against the currently published version.
No version combination causes a captured value, photograph, scan, or signature to be discarded.
A model-version change never alters the outcome of a specification check, a severity classification, a gate decision, or a hold.
No device adopts a new application version inside an active run; adoption occurs at a run boundary or while no run is active.
business_rules.enforcement_point: device command application at execution boundary

business_rules.statement: The application-version floor cannot be raised without an impact statement naming the affected device count by tenant, and the raise requires Admin approval.
Adoption first, floor second, is the only safe order on a fleet that is legitimately offline for hours at a time.
Rollback is refused where any irreversible lifecycle effect has executed since the release, with the specific effects listed from the audit log.
No rollback path deletes any record; supersession and compensating actions are the only permitted corrections.
Every migration declares its reversibility at build time, and the rollback record displays that declaration rather than asking for a judgement.
Safe read-only mode permits in-flight runs to complete, capture, sync, compute summaries, and close, and blocks authoring, configuration, and creation of Jobs and runs.
Safe read-only mode never presents itself to a worker as a compliance suspension, and the compliance-suspension message is reserved for its own state.
Raising the application-version floor is never described on any surface as having updated any device.
No rollout or rollback event changes anything on a device that is offline, and no surface shows such a device as pending, lagging, or updated.
A release cannot be declared complete while any conformance assertion has failed.
A restore re-applies completed anonymisation events and re-establishes legal holds before any lifecycle scheduler resumes.
Business state and audit entries are restored together; a restore that would separate them is refused.

Every requirement carries at least one acceptance criterion, and every acceptance criterion carries at least one test. Every test links back to at least one requirement. A requirement with no acceptance criterion is rejected at review; a test with no requirement is rejected at review.
business_rules.enforcement_point: traceability conformance check; build fails before functional tests run

business_rules.statement: No capability — atom, agent, or composed behaviour — is enabled while its evaluation scenarios are pending or failing. This is a platform invariant with no off position for any account including the Root Super Admin.
A test that exercises a contradiction recorded in the contradictions register does not resolve it. It asserts both readings separately and reports which one the build implements.
Coverage is never reported as complete while an open decision remains open. The coverage report carries an explicit "blocked by decision" column.
No test may create, alter, or delete data in a production tenant.

A requirement may not be marked implemented on the strength of a code change; it is marked implemented when its acceptance criteria pass. A test may not be marked passing against a criterion it does not name. A criterion may not be deleted while its requirement lives.

decisions.question: Latency and responsiveness targets
options: defer until the device profile lands
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopt as engineering targets now; convert to contractual after validation on representative hardware
decisions.impact: Constrains rendering-mechanism decision (engineering item E2), device spec and pre-staging budget

decisions.question: Availability, Recovery Time Objective, Recovery Point Objective, backup frequency and retention
decisions.adopted_working_position: 99.5 per cent monthly for web surfaces, higher for capture ingestion; 4-hour and 1-hour Recovery Time Objectives; 15-minute server-side Recovery Point Objective
decisions.status: open — recommendation only; called the single most commercially significant open value in the blueprint
decisions.impact: Blocks every service-level conversation and commercial commitment

decisions.question: Scale envelope: tenants, devices, concurrency, throughput, peak ratio
decisions.adopted_working_position: Derive from the pipeline and re-derive quarterly
decisions.impact: Blocks capacity planning and load testing target

decisions.question: Maintenance-window shape and duration
decisions.adopted_working_position: Monthly, announced, outside every tenant's shift where the timezone spread allows
decisions.impact: Blocks release process before the first tenant goes live

decisions.question: Device storage budgets: queue, media, pre-staging, and the sync drain target
decisions.adopted_working_position: Derive from the profile; at least one full shift of captures and media on the minimum specification
decisions.impact: Blocks pre-staging and media budgets; competes for one storage pool

decisions.question: Object-durability class
decisions.adopted_working_position: Provider-managed storage at its published durability class, stated honestly
decisions.impact: Blocks storage and backup design before infrastructure procurement

decisions.question: Accessibility standard, contrast, touch-target size, task-success target
options: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 level AA
decisions.adopted_working_position: Level AA for the four web surfaces; enhanced contrast and an 11-millimetre minimum target for floor-facing controls
decisions.impact: Blocks design system before interface build

decisions.question: Offline language packaging, locale formatting, translation turnaround
decisions.adopted_working_position: Carry the assigned worker's language; interacts with DEC-WIDIFF-001 on difficulty levels
decisions.impact: Blocks package contract; package size competes with media budget

decisions.question: Operating-system version floor, app-version floor and grace period, battery target
decisions.adopted_working_position: Two most recent major versions; a stated grace period before floor enforcement
decisions.impact: Wide floor increases test matrix and security exposure

decisions.question: Observability thresholds, metrics and log retention, sampling rate, non-occurrence detection
decisions.adopted_working_position: Set below the tested capacity ceiling; full trace capture for gated and failed runs
decisions.impact: Blocks alerting design before production launch

decisions.question: Release cadence, test-coverage floor, deprecation notice, export format
decisions.adopted_working_position: A regular announced cadence; a coverage floor for the deterministic layer; a stated deprecation notice period
decisions.impact: Blocks release and deprecation process

decisions.question: Sync ordering on reconnection: captures versus commands
options: Safety reading: commands first, so a suspension, wipe, or hold lands before more work
Integrity reading: captures first, so unsynced evidence is never at risk
decisions.adopted_working_position: Stop class first, then the full capture upload, then the enabling class
decisions.status: adopted working position, 2026-08-14, ratification owed; both source readings preserved in the card
decisions.impact: Blocks sync engine design; build proceeds on the adopted order meanwhile

decisions.question: Storage-full behaviour on the device
decisions.status: carried — explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification; no behaviour may be invented
decisions.impact: Highest-priority open item in the offline family; unstated behaviour could cost evidence

decisions.question: Standardised device profile: make and class, capability tier, operating-system split
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until it lands, the working floor is a sensible mainstream Android and iOS specification
decisions.impact: Every client-side performance and storage target rests on it

decisions.question: Scanner hardware list
decisions.impact: Untested scanner families make the fast path slow on day one

decisions.question: Record-finish window bounds
decisions.adopted_working_position: Default 48 hours; bounds 24 hours to 7 days
decisions.impact: Governs late-arrival folding and audited recompute

decisions.question: Archived-data retrieval expectation
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommend a stated business-hours target once the tiering design is fixed
decisions.status: carried — stated as open at drafting
decisions.impact: Drives archive tier choice and cost curve

decisions.question: Certifications and ITAR intent
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopt as stated; claim nothing beyond the Certification-Support Matrix
decisions.impact: A genuine ITAR commitment implies US-persons-only operations and a forked deployment topology

decisions.question: Three-stage approval chain versus Lane B auto-publish
decisions.status: carried contradiction — neither reading is adopted
decisions.impact: Leaves the auto-publish-versus-three-stage tension unresolved

decisions.question: Composed-agent lifecycle: deprecation, rollback and the fate of in-flight runs
decisions.impact: Composed-agent deprecation and rollback undefined

decisions.question: Difficulty-level packaging: all levels or only the assigned worker's
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until resolved, the package definition carries all levels
decisions.impact: Package size unbounded against the media budget

decisions.question: Metrics retention, service-level-objective targets, sampling rate, log level, recovery objectives for observability
decisions.impact: Values have no source in the Statement of Work; controls render awaiting-decision

decisions.question: Platform on-call mechanism, rota and acknowledgement path for the 120-minute escalation
decisions.impact: The 120-minute on-call escalation has no defined mechanism in the source

decisions.question: Queue retry limits, back-off schedule, dead-letter thresholds, queue ceilings and scheduler-health thresholds
options: too few retries discards recoverable work
too many hide a broken dependency behind an infinite loop
decisions.impact: Opposite failure modes; infinite retry is prohibited by the fallback discipline

decisions.question: Consequences of repeated tenant-initiated session termination, platform notification of it, and support Recovery Time Objective
decisions.adopted_working_position: The blueprint recommends failing closed
decisions.impact: Whether an in-flight read is aborted mid-response is unstated

decisions.question: Platform incident severity ladder definitions and response-time commitments
decisions.adopted_working_position: Four platform incident levels proposed, deliberately distinct from the tenant-facing deviation Severity catalog
decisions.impact: Level definitions determine communication obligations that may have contractual weight

decisions.question: Wipe reaching an offline or unreachable device when a final sync attempt is required first
decisions.impact: An unreachable device cannot satisfy the final-sync precondition for a critical-class wipe

decisions.question: Staged rollout, canary, health-based abort, and automatic rollback scope
options: rely only on release channels and the app-version floor
decisions.status: open — decision owner client's platform lead with Root Super Admin approval
decisions.impact: Rings, canaries, and multi-environment parity are real infrastructure and operating expense

decisions.question: Environment inventory (development, test, staging, sandbox, production)
options: Production plus one non-production parity environment
decisions.adopted_working_position: Propose a minimum inventory of production plus one non-production parity environment
decisions.impact: The word environment appears once, as a setting, with no enumeration

decisions.question: Backup frequency and retention, restore procedure, tested restore, RTO, RPO, regional failover
options: continuous in-region replication with fast failover
cross-region replication with a declared failover region
decisions.adopted_working_position: Continuous in-region replication plus periodic backup with a tested restore on a stated cadence, deferring cross-region failover until region-per-tenant leaves the roadmap
decisions.status: open — no number proposed for RTO/RPO
decisions.impact: A stated Recovery Time Objective drives the whole deployment topology

decisions.question: What 'out of policy' means for a device below the application-version floor: refused sync, refused new assignment, or refused execution
decisions.adopted_working_position: Preserved rather than decided; under every reading captured work is never discarded
decisions.impact: Bears directly on offline device behaviour through rollout and rollback

decisions.question: Capture-type set divergence
decisions.adopted_working_position: The §5.5.3 seven
decisions.status: adopted 2026-08-14, both source readings preserved in the card
decisions.impact: A Frontline player cannot render a type the contract does not name

decisions.question: Authority tension: Atom Registry engineering capability enablement versus generic tenant feature-value authority in the Tenant-Configuration Registry
decisions.status: open — DEC-FEAT-001 through DEC-FEAT-005, not resolved here
decisions.impact: Two competing configuration surfaces; a careless feature-flag system could weaken the floor register

decisions.question: Precedence of tier entitlements against tenant overrides
decisions.impact: Commercial feature gating precedence undefined

decisions.question: Identity of the acceptance authority who signs the acceptance report
decisions.status: open — not specified in the Statement of Work
decisions.impact: No named signer for release acceptance

decisions.question: Audit tamper-evidence posture
decisions.adopted_working_position: Not available at V1; compensating controls recommended
decisions.status: carried — deferred beyond V1 by the source
decisions.impact: An integrity exception cannot be distinguished from an alteration by the platform alone

decisions.question: Whether trace access requires an access class
decisions.impact: Traces may contain tenant operational content, retained 24 months

decisions.question: Time to contain a Severity A security incident (target)
decisions.impact: Containment speed depends on DEC-SEC-023 pre-authorised containment

decisions.question: Tenant notification time after confirmed exposure
decisions.impact: A short deadline may force notification before facts are established

decisions.question: Scheduled-work timeliness tolerance, misfire policy and maximum lateness
decisions.adopted_working_position: Per scheduler policy as recommended
decisions.impact: Without it, 'late' is undefined and no reconciliation can flag it

decisions.question: Exactly-once effect guarantee mechanism
decisions.adopted_working_position: Guaranteed by idempotency keys and leases
decisions.impact: Deduplication requires a store with its own retention

decisions.question: Concurrency per scheduler
options: One occurrence at a time for lifecycle jobs
decisions.adopted_working_position: One occurrence at a time for lifecycle jobs; bounded parallelism for per-tenant jobs
decisions.impact: Serial execution is slow at scale; parallel execution risks overlap

objects.name: Scheduled execution occurrence
key_relationships: carries the Schedule Definition version that produced it
carries an idempotency key derived from definition identifier and due moment
claimed by a lease with a fencing token

objects.name: Support session
key_relationships: mirrors into the tenant audit stream
renders a tenant banner with End-session control
appears in Platform Access History permanently

objects.name: Release record
key_relationships: backup status with last tested restore date

objects.name: Rollback decision record
key_relationships: lists every irreversible effect executed since the release from the audit log

objects.name: Work package
key_relationships: pinned per run and never re-based
per-device package inventory with per-run pinned versions
adoption-timing lag measured only for runs started after publication

workflows.name: How a performance target is set and validated
workflows.trigger: The client's device profile lands, closing DEC-DEVICE-001
terminal_states: targets become contractual
targets renegotiated with a stated reason
re-validated at each device-fleet refresh

workflows.name: Capacity management as a recurring act
workflows.trigger: Commercial pipeline states the expected tenant set
terminal_states: envelope re-derived at each commercial milestone and each device-fleet refresh

workflows.name: An outage from the floor's point of view
workflows.trigger: The platform becomes unavailable at 09:30
terminal_states: queued captures drain in order on restoration
late arrivals fold in flagged late_arrival
audited recompute after finish

workflows.name: A device's offline endurance, end to end
workflows.trigger: Device syncs at 06:02 then loses connectivity
terminal_states: new run starts refused at trust-window expiry
storage-full behaviour deferred as DEC-STORE-001
queue drains on reconnection

workflows.name: Proving a fifteen-year-old record
workflows.trigger: An auditor asks for the torque record on RB-0007 from August 2026
terminal_states: record produced with pinned version, evidence, audit and decision record
retrieved from archive at the DEC-RETRIEVE-001 expectation

workflows.name: Publishing in two languages
workflows.trigger: An author writes the work instruction in one language at one difficulty level
terminal_states: publication fails on untranslated keys
publication and pinning at run assignment

workflows.name: From device profile to published specification
workflows.trigger: Client delivers the standardised device profile
terminal_states: minimum device specification published
repeats at each fleet refresh, roughly every two years

workflows.name: How a problem becomes visible
workflows.trigger: A device's sync health degrades
terminal_states: announcement console communication, type incident

contradictions.description: Service-level-objective targets are offered as a console control for a figure the contract never fixes.
conflicting_values: a settings control exists for SLO targets `[SoW Fact — §8.7.1 Observability]`
no value is given anywhere in the Statement of Work

contradictions.description: Sync ordering on reconnection: the source explicitly defers it and two readings conflict.
conflicting_values: Safety reading: commands first, so a suspension, wipe, or hold lands before more work
Integrity reading: captures first, so unsynced evidence is never at risk

contradictions.description: The three-stage Studio approval chain conflicts with Lane B auto-publish; the blueprint states neither reading is adopted.
conflicting_values: Author, then a different Reviewer, then the Release Authority `[§5.11.1]`
approval auto-publishes a patch-class change `[§3.8]`

contradictions.description: Capture-type set divergence: a Frontline player cannot render a type the contract does not name.
conflicting_values: the §5.5.3 seven (adopted 2026-08-14)
the divergent capture-type set preserved in the card

contradictions.description: Device wipe is critical-class and requires a final sync attempt first, which an unreachable device cannot satisfy.
conflicting_values: wipe requires a final sync attempt `[§8.13.3]`
the device is unreachable beyond the 72-hour ceiling and cannot sync

contradictions.description: Feature authority tension between Atom Registry per-tenant capability enablement and the Tenant-Configuration Registry's platform-side authority over tenant current values.
conflicting_values: per-tenant capability enablement in the Atom Registry `[§8.2.2]`
platform-side changes to tenant current values as console actions `[§8.19]`

contradictions.description: The capture-state prose list includes "uploaded" but the capture state machine diagram omits it, going from Uploading straight to ServerReceived.
conflicting_values: prose list of thirteen capture states including "uploaded"
diagram states: CommittedLocally, Queued, Uploading, UploadInterrupted, ServerReceived, Validated, ...

contradictions.description: Key management and artifact signing is assigned two priorities at once in the prioritisation matrix.
conflicting_values: 2 by consequence
10 by visibility

contradictions.description: A canary cohort is available in substance for the mobile application but not for server behaviour, so 'roll out to ten percent of tenants' is answerable only in half.
conflicting_values: mobile: release channels permit a per-fleet staged rollout today
server: every tenant shares one deployment; percentage rollout requires infrastructure not in scope

contradictions.description: Sandbox-before-publish is easy to mistake for a staging environment but is only a publication gate; reading it as an environment commitment would be an over-claim.
conflicting_values: sandbox-before-publish is an enforced invariant `[§8.7.4]`
no environment inventory is specified anywhere

failures_fallbacks.trigger: sustained latency beyond thresholds — the platform is slow rather than down
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: shed load in reverse order of safety importance: reports and analytics first, agent operations second, oversight refresh third
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the Command Center degrades to a stated reduced-freshness mode; Frontline continues entirely unaffected
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the floor keeps working and keeps capturing; oversight is delayed and says it is delayed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: queued captures drain in order; late arrivals inside the record-finish window fold in flagged late_arrival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: queue depth or latency beyond thresholds — demand exceeds capacity
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: back-pressure at the sync endpoint with client-side exponential backoff and jitter
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: accept captures and commands only, refusing all other traffic with an honest message
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: capture ingestion and command delivery only; every other surface degraded and labelled
failures_fallbacks.recovery: queues drain in order; envelope re-derived with the observed peak

failures_fallbacks.trigger: platform unavailability
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the offline-first architecture, automatic
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: where the outage outlasts the offline trust window, devices stop accepting new run starts and the plant falls back to its own procedure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: frozen lots stay frozen; parked runs stay parked; committed captures stay committed and queued; nothing is approved, released, cleared or published
failures_fallbacks.recovery: stop-class commands, then queued captures upload in full, then enabling-class commands, per DEC-SYNC-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: window expiry, storage threshold, or a persistent skew event
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: walk the device into coverage; reassign runs to a device in coverage
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the plant falls back to its own procedure for the remainder of the outage
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the device retains everything captured and accepts nothing new; it must never silently become 'the device drops the oldest capture'
failures_fallbacks.recovery: queue drains in order; conflicts route per the skew guard; late arrivals fold in

failures_fallbacks.trigger: an integrity-canary failure or a failed retrieval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retrieve from a replica or backup
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: record an explicit integrity exception with its scope named to the tenant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: affected scope marked as an integrity exception and placed under legal hold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: an integrity report enumerating every affected record

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a pilot finding or a correction-rate signal
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: adjust the interface within the responsive design without changing behaviour
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the tenant reverts the affected steps to a supervisor-witnessed procedure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the affected step type is not executed on the affected device class
failures_fallbacks.recovery: re-validation on the affected hardware under the plant's own conditions

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a failed completeness check or a runtime missing-key event
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: publication is refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the device shows the key's identifier rather than a wrong-language string and reports it as an operational event
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the affected content is not published and the affected workers are not assigned to it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the variant authored and the check passing

failures_fallbacks.trigger: telemetry showing devices below the floor
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: notify the Tenant Admin with the specific devices and versions
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the tenant runs on fewer devices while replacements arrive; supervisor reassigns runs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: non-conformant devices do not start new work; work already under way completes and syncs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: on update or replacement the device re-enrolls or resumes; device audit trail records the transition

failures_fallbacks.trigger: telemetry gap beyond a threshold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: fall back to a secondary signal, e.g. ingestion volume as a proxy for fleet health
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: rely on tenant reports through support and say so in the incident record
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: all monitoring surfaces explicitly labelled unavailable; incidents handled reactively
failures_fallbacks.recovery: buffered telemetry back-fills; the gap period is marked in metric history

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a reconciliation failure or lateness beyond tolerance
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: run late where the misfire policy says late is better than never
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: formal abandonment with a recorded reason — correct for a digest, not for anonymisation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the scheduler paused with every deferred occurrence enumerated
failures_fallbacks.recovery: every deferred occurrence executed, backfilled or abandoned with a reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a detected misclassification or a harmful change
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: publish a superseding version — AVIIXA has no rollback in the ordinary sense
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: compliance-level intervention through the platform's own containment levers
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the affected work is not executed; runs already under way finish on their pinned version
failures_fallbacks.recovery: the superseding version published and distributed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: blind operation — the platform runs while nobody can tell whether it is running correctly
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: fall back to the audit log and the surfaces' own freshness markers
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the console itself unavailable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the deterministic on-device layer continues unchanged; gates, specification checks, severity classification and the Severity 1 hold have no off switch
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restoration of collection plus verification that outage-window aggregates are marked incomplete rather than zero

failures_fallbacks.trigger: collector unavailability beyond one refresh interval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: buffer at the emitter for a bounded period and mark the window incomplete
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: console banner: platform telemetry is degraded; health values shown are older than their refresh interval
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: observability is dark; the audit log continues under the one-transaction guarantee; the deterministic layer continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore collection, verify one clean cycle, then lift the banner; rebuild aggregates from audit labelled reconstructed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: absence of a layer's signals for one refresh interval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: derive the missing layer's state from the adjacent layer's evidence and label it derived
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: declare an observability incident and operate from tenant reports and the audit log
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: floor operation continues offline-first; the platform team operates blind on that layer with the fact stated on the console
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore emitters, verify two clean intervals, clear derived labels, replay device audit trails

failures_fallbacks.trigger: ingestion or dispatch unavailability, or pending duration crossing the alert threshold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retry with back-off inside the configured limit, resuming from the interruption point
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: dead-letter the individual item with its reason, keep the item, raise it for human resolution; never delete it
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the device continues capturing locally with its deterministic safety layer intact; sync health reported as degraded with the pending duration named
failures_fallbacks.recovery: drain queues, verify integrity, confirm command acknowledgements, reconcile device ledger against server accepted set

failures_fallbacks.trigger: two consecutive failures of a definition, or a lease reclaim that finds a partially applied effect
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retry within the configured limit with back-off, preserving the idempotency key
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: pause the definition, quarantine its pending occurrences, and raise an incident
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: definition paused, every unrun occurrence retained as an explicit missed record; for anonymisation and tiering 'not yet performed', never 'partially performed'
failures_fallbacks.recovery: verify the reconciliation report is clean, then resume through approval

failures_fallbacks.trigger: missing propagation stamps for one refresh interval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: reconstruct the missing stamps from the audit log
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: suppress the aggregate lag figure entirely for the affected window and state why
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the hold itself remains in force wherever it was placed; the platform reports that it cannot currently measure propagation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore instrumentation, recompute from audit for the window

failures_fallbacks.trigger: delivery failures beyond one evaluation cycle
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: in-app delivery continues when email fails and vice versa
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: out-of-band on-call arrangement, TBD under DEC-OBS-002
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: alerting is dark; tenant-visible protocol banners still fire; the deterministic on-device layer is untouched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore delivery, replay undelivered alerts marked delayed with their original detection time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: banner or mirror confirmation failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retry banner and mirror confirmation once within a short bounded window
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: terminate a live session that loses mirroring, recording actions taken before the loss, and notify the tenant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: no platform-side access into tenant context is possible, including the compliance-emergency path
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore mirroring, verify with a test session against an internal fixture tenant, then re-enable

failures_fallbacks.trigger: incident declaration
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: communicate on the remaining channel of the two if the announcement console is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: if the approval cycle is unavailable, no change is applied; the platform remains degraded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform in stated degraded mode; floor operating offline-first; audit intact; tenants informed of what is unavailable and what is unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: verification complete and reconciliation clean

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a release that changes what the floor is doing
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: pinning makes most releases inert for in-flight work by construction
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: rollback impossible because a migration is irreversible
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform read-only or unavailable with honest messaging; Frontline continues offline-first on staged packages
failures_fallbacks.recovery: verified against the deployment-conformance tests; reconciliation repairs duplicate or missing official effects

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a release-attributed defect confirmed by observability
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: roll back the server version
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: safe read-only mode
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform read-only with honest messaging; floor continuing offline-first on staged packages
failures_fallbacks.recovery: rollback or fix-forward under approval, then conformance verification

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a definition-attributed anomaly
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: pause the definition, recording skipped-by-pause occurrences
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: retire the definition and handle its effect manually — acceptable for run auto-close and tiering, explicitly not for anonymisation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: definition paused or retired; no effect performed; every unrun occurrence explicitly recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: a corrected version approved and a clean reconciliation report

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a fencing rejection on an effect that had already partially applied, or evidence of two leaders
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: lease renewal during long effects, with the effect abandoning itself if renewal fails rather than continuing unfenced
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: pause the definition and require human resolution — mandatory for anonymisation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: no effect performed; occurrence recorded as failed with reason class; downstream state unchanged
failures_fallbacks.recovery: verified single leader plus clean reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a validation failure attributable to version mismatch
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: accept the capture and quarantine it with the reason 'definition version unresolved'
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: route the quarantined item to the Command Center's conflict-and-skew review for a Quality Manager decision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the capture sits quarantined, visible, undeleted, and excluded from summaries until decided
failures_fallbacks.recovery: restore the definition version from the registry, release the quarantine and reconcile

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a soak-window signal breach or a tenant report
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: halt the rollout at its current stage
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: lower the application-version floor to the previous value under maker-checker so reverted devices are not out of policy
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the fleet split across two application versions, both above the floor, with the split visible on the compatibility view
failures_fallbacks.recovery: remediate, re-canary, widen again; reconcile per-device version and package inventory

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a failed rollback attempt
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: retry the rollback once with the same evidence and the same approval
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: complete forward to a fixed version rather than continuing to fight a partially applied reversal
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform read-only or unavailable, honestly messaged; Frontline continuing offline-first with full deterministic safety
failures_fallbacks.recovery: forward or reverted, then verified by the conformance suite and release-window reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.trigger: a version mismatch detected at sync
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: the device that adopted a reverted version simply reverts at its next sync
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: the device is placed below floor deliberately, its captures accepted and quarantined if necessary
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: the device holds its work locally with deterministic safety intact; captures quarantined rather than rejected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: device updated by the tenant, queue drained, quarantine released

failures_fallbacks.trigger: loss of the primary datastore or regional impairment
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: in-region replica promotion, which preserves residency
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: safe read-only mode while restore proceeds
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: platform unavailable with honest messaging; Frontline continuing offline-first with full deterministic safety including on-device severity classification and the Severity 1 hold

failures_fallbacks.trigger: the traceability generator cannot produce an index
